description: Cross-paper conclusion confidence rubric for the Phase 5 conclusion-synthesis pipeline (app/services/conclusion_grader.py). Unlike paper_grading_rubric.json (which scores one paper in isolation), this rubric scores one synthesized *claim* — e.g. 'Improves deep sleep duration' — built up across every graded paper (grade_score > 50) that discusses it. Three categories summing to a maximum of 100 points, mapped to letter grades A-E.

grade_bands.label: Very high confidence — strong, consistent, well-specified evidence
High confidence — good evidence with minor gaps
Moderate confidence — plausible but limited or mixed evidence
Low confidence — weak, thin, or inconsistent evidence
Very low confidence — minimal, contradicted, or vague evidence

categories.label: Source Evidence Strength
categories.description: How strong the underlying paper(s) supporting this claim are, based on their own paper_grading_rubric.json grade_score (study design, journal rigor, sample methodology, funding bias). For a brand-new claim this reflects the single paper introducing it; for a merged claim it isn't re-scored on every merge (see conclusion_grader.py) — only cross_paper_consensus is re-evaluated as more papers come in.

score_tiers.example: Primarily backed by paper(s) graded 'A' (85-100) — systematic reviews or well-controlled human RCTs
Primarily backed by paper(s) graded 'B' (70-84) — solid methodology, minor limitations
Primarily backed by paper(s) graded 'C' (50-69) — fair quality or notable limitations
Backed by a single borderline paper just above the grading threshold
Evidence quality unclear or minimally documented

categories.label: Cross-Paper Consensus
categories.description: How many independent papers support vs. contradict this claim, and how consistent the finding is across them. Re-evaluated by Gemini every time a new qualifying paper is merged into an existing claim (see conclusion_grader.py::process_paper_conclusions) — this is the one category score that changes after a claim is first created.

score_tiers.example: Supported by 4+ independent papers with no contradicting evidence
Supported by 2-3 independent papers, no contradicting evidence
Supported by a single paper so far, or supported by multiple with one contradicting outlier
Mixed evidence — roughly as many contradicting papers as supporting ones
Contradicted by more papers than currently support it

categories.label: Claim Specificity & Clinical Relevance
categories.description: How precisely the claim specifies dosage, population, and outcome measure, and how clinically actionable it is for someone deciding whether to take this ingredient.

score_tiers.example: Specific dosage, population, and outcome measure all clearly stated
Dosage and outcome stated, population described only generally
Partial specificity — dosage OR outcome stated, but not both
Vague claim with minimal specific detail
No specific dosage, population, or outcome detail provided
